 Score Predictions: Can Sunderland Start Climbing The Table At The CBS?
 Can the Lads pick up three valuable points and kickstart their league campaign in the Midlands?
 by Malcolm Dugdale , Martin Wanless , Will Jones , Matthew Foster , Anthony Gair , Gary Winter , and Jack Howe-gingell Oct 31, 2026, 5:00 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Daniel Ballard celebrates as his header goes in off the crossbar to put Sunderland through to Wembley for the Championship Play-off Final during the Sky Bet Championship Play-off Semi-final Second Leg match between Sunderland and Coventry City at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, England, on May 13, 2025. (Photo by Scott Llewellyn | MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) NurPhoto via Getty Images Stats at a glance: Coventry City (A) Premier League: 31/10/2026
 Average home goals predicted: 0.75 
 Average away goals predicted: 2.4 
 Confidence of Roker Report’s writers: 7/10 
 Predicting a win for the Lads: 87.5% 
 Martin Wanless (Cautious Optimist) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 2 
 While it’s technically not a must win, it’s an “it would be really, really, really beneficial if we could win” — and it’s a game I really want us to win too, for a number of reasons. 
 Coventry haven’t been in the best of form at all – neither have we, of course – and with their only home win coming thanks to thumping Newcastle we do need to be aware of their attacking ability. 
 However, we’ve almost got a full squad back after being pretty badly hit by injuries over the past month or so, and with a few more attacking options staking their claim for game time of some description thanks to strong displays on Wednesday, we’ve got more attacking prowess than any of us probably thought we had this time last week. 
 That said, it’ll be a tight game. Their fans, for whatever reason, froth when we come to town so it’l. be a good atmosphere and I reckon we’ll come out with a much-needed three points. 
 Key differentiator: I think the leadership of Thomas Meunier, who I expect to be back in the team, will be crucial. 
 Confidence: 5/10 
 Bold call: Both sides to have a player sent off. 
 MOENCHENGLADBACH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 27: Referee Florian Lechner shows the red card during the DFB Cup 2026/27 match between Borussia Mönchengladbach and Karlsruher SC at ista-Borussia-Park on October 27, 2026 in Moenchengladbach, Germany. (Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images) Getty Images Malc Dugdale (Scarred happy clapper) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 0 Sunderland 2 
 Coventry have been shipping goals for fun and not scoring many in most games — apart from against the filth, but we know how crap they are, whereas we scored three with our second team in the cup against a decent less-rotated Brentford side. 
 I’m hopeful we can keep a clean sheet and get a couple of goals early in the game to kill the crowd and take this home with a controlled performance after half time. 
 Key differentiator: Brian Brobbey is back and rested, and we have competition for places starting to ramp up big time, including out wide. I think our depth and rising confidence will be the difference today. 
 Confidence: 6/10 
 Bold call: 0-2 in the first half then a shut out for the second to take all three points home. 
 SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 25: Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Leeds United at Stadium of Light on October 25, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Getty Images Jack Howe-Gingell (Eternal optimist) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 3 
 After a fun game against Brentford in midweek that saw us progress to the next stage, we must take that confidence into this one. Coventry will see us as a beatable opponent but we need to remind them how tough we are. 
 A promising display against a strong Brentford team not only provided some food for thought for Régis Le Bris but yet another platform to spring from. 
 We must take advantage and get the season back on track. 
 Key differentiator: They’ll have an arrogance that’ll play against them, and we’ll pick them off. 
 Confidence: 9/10 
 Bold call: Two of our goals to be deemed own goals. 
 Frank Lampard, manager of Coventry City, gestures during the Premier League match between Coventry City and Fulham at the Coventry Building Society Arena in Coventry, on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) NurPhoto via Getty Images “Champion” Will Jones (Heart over head) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 3 
 That Brentford game was much more like it. 
 A 3-2 win, a proper performance and hopefully a bit of momentum to take into Saturday. The rotation clearly didn’t stop us getting the job done, and there should be plenty of confidence going into Coventry. 
 Coventry are a tough side on their own patch, but after Wednesday, I fancy us to carry that attacking intent into the league. 
 If we start quickly and get them on the back foot, there’s no reason we can’t come away with all three points. I’m going for a big away win. 
 Key differentiator: Taking the confidence from Brentford into the game and making our chances count. 
 Confidence: 7/10 
 Bold call: There will be two goals in the first ten minutes. 
 SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Jules Ahoka of Sunderland is challenged by Mikkel Damsgaard of Brentford during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Sunderland and Brentford at Stadium of Light on October 28, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Getty Images Matty Foster (Pragmatist) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 2 
 I don’t want to be that guy and call this a ‘must win’, but it would certainly go a long way in helping our current position in the league, given where Coventry find themselves too. 
 This is our first meeting since that magical night at the Stadium of Light, and Coventry will want revenge. 
 Add to that the ‘rivalry’ that’s built up over the years. 
 Key differentiator: The team is starting to regain some strength with players returning from injury, and that’s vital for us. 
 Confidence: 6/10 
 Bold call: History will repeat itself in that one of our goals comes from a defensive gaffe from a Coventry player. 
 Anthony Gair (Depreciating optimist) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 0 Sunderland 4 
 We’re going to run rampant at the Ricoh Arena (or whatever it’s called these days).
 Jimmy Hill will turn in his grave at how poor Frank Lampard’s Coventry will be, and we’ll kickstart our season in the most prolific fashion. 
 Key differentiator: The press from the front will force multiple errors from Coventry. 
 Confidence: 10/10 
 Bold call: We’ll have more than five corners in the first half. 
 Coventry City FC manager Jimmy Hill, seated, with his team, December 3rd 1961. Hill is also chairman of the PFA (Professional Footballers’ Association). (Photo by Daily Express/Hulton Archive/Getty Images) Getty Images Gary Winter (Glass almost empty) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 1 
 I’m going to refrain from using the term ‘must-win’ now, as there are are too many points still to play for, and a good run of form can elevate a team quickly to mid-table. 
 However, a win today would be a huge boost whilst landing a blow on a fellow struggler, and would give the Lads a platform and some much-needed belief following the excellent League Cup victory. 
 Key differentiator: I’m not sure where the attacking quality displayed at Brentford and Man City away has disappeared to, but the League Cup win aside, we’re generally playing without belief and often with fear. 
 If that belief turns up today, we’ll win, but unfortunately league position can be psychologically very damaging and we’re starting to play very much like the twentieth best team. 
 Confidence: 6/10 
 Bold call: All goalscorers will also end the game with a yellow card. 
 Brett Lyons-Davis (Gut feeling guy) says…
 Score prediction: Coventry 1 Sunderland 2 
 Oh good. It’s time to renew our rivalry with Coventry in match that for me is must-win.
 With Sunderland unbeaten in three, the green shoots are starting to come up and I think the lads will avoid any Halloween horror show. 
 Key differentiator: Feels like our confidence and team spirit is getting stronger each game. 
 Confidence: 7/10 
 Bold call: Wilson Isidor comes off the bench and scores the winner. 
 Last game thoughts…
 The cup game was a real breath of fresh air for me and listening to our pods for a lot of the lads too.
 Mass rotation often leads to pandemonium, but the score probably flattered Brentford who rotated far less. We unearthed a raft of competition for places, and some genuine talent out wide may well be used from today.
 Coventry isn’t a place we generally do well at (ignoring a couple of Mays ago), but they’re really struggling with both scoring and defending, and we’re hopefully on the way up while encouraging today’s hosts to head down the way.
 Vitaly Janelt of Brentford FC is put under pressure by Jocelin Ta Bi of Sunderland AFC during the Carabao Cup Round of 16 match between Sunderland and Brentford at the Stadium Of Light in Sunderland, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) NurPhoto via Getty Images Last game predictions…
 Four of the lads went for a draw and penalties to decide the cup game, and could not have been further off the mark really.
 Jack and Gair called a win but neither got the exact score — though if you combined their joint scores, you could not get any closer.
 SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Mikkel Damsgaard of Brentford is challenged by Alan Browne of Sunderland during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Sunderland and Brentford at Stadium of Light on October 28, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Getty Images Predictions table and standings
 With only one point scored for two of the writers, the table stays the same but Jack closes the gap on Brett a little, and Gair gets a point closer to second place.
 How the points are awarded 
 Just a quick reminder of how we allocate points to our match-by-match predictions:
 Correct score = Three points 
 Correct outcome (but not correct score) = One point 
 Correct Bold Call = One point 
 Possible deductions for repeatedly not submitting on time = a two-point deduction.
